songs.title: Paper Satellites
songs.description: Piano, acoustic guitar and a hopeful chorus about finding your way home.

request.style: English, warm acoustic pop, intimate clear female vocals, acoustic guitar, soft piano, gentle live drums, hopeful chorus, 92 BPM, complete song with a short instrumental outro
request.lyrics:
[Verse]
I folded up a map of where we'd been
And tucked it in the pocket of my jeans
The station clock was running out of light
You said the longest roads can turn out right

[Chorus]
We are paper satellites
Finding home in borrowed light
Every road and every mile
Brings me closer to your smile

[Verse]
The morning paints the windows amber gold
A thousand little stories left untold
I trace the towns like freckles on your hand
And find my way across this paper land

[Chorus]
We are paper satellites
Finding home in borrowed light
Every road and every mile
Brings me closer to your smile

[Outro]
Finding home in borrowed light

songs.title: After the Last Train
songs.description: A late-night city song with pulsing synths, a steady beat and a bright refrain.

request.style: English, melodic synth pop, expressive male vocals, analog synthesizer arpeggios, warm synth bass, crisp electronic drums, wide atmospheric pads, nostalgic but uplifting, 112 BPM, complete song
request.lyrics:
[Verse]
The last train leaves a silver line
Between your street and mine
The city hums a quiet tune

[Pre-Chorus]
No timetable can tell us where to go
We follow all the little lights we know

[Chorus]
After the last train
We'll dance beneath the rain
With nowhere we must be
And every road set free
After the last train

[Verse]
Your shadow moves across the wall
I catch it when you call
The traffic sings in distant keys
Our song rides on the breeze

[Chorus]
After the last train
We'll dance beneath the rain
With nowhere we must be
And every road set free
After the last train
Let's find our names again

[Outro]
We'll find our names again

songs.title: Lanterns on the River
songs.description: A gentle folk arrangement with fingerpicked guitar and a river-town story.

request.style: English, intimate folk ballad, clear warm female lead voice, fingerpicked acoustic guitar, soft upright bass, brushed percussion, delicate violin, natural acoustic sound, reflective and hopeful, 78 BPM, complete song
request.lyrics:
[Verse]
There's a bridge beside the water
Where the willow branches lean
And the boats return at sundown
From the places we have seen

[Chorus]
Set a lantern on the river
Let it carry what we know
All the words we never managed
All the things we couldn't show

[Verse]
You were humming in the kitchen
With the window open wide
And the summer kept a promise
In the turning of the tide

[Chorus]
Set a lantern on the river
Let it carry what we know
All the words we never managed
All the things we couldn't show

[Outro]
When the morning finds the water
We will let the lantern go

[Verse]

[Chorus]
